Truth is our most essential tool for engaging with the markets and constantly improving because once you know what’s true about your problems and opportunities, you can determine how to get better. Valuing truth means being transparent about your decision-making and mistakes, giving and receiving feedback with humility, and fighting for the best answers over hierarchy, ego, or self-interest. Operating this way is hard – it’s only possible because we build meaning in our work and relationships. This meaning comes from the audacity of the mission, and the joy of working alongside people who make you a better version of yourself. The culture, like Bridgewater itself, is always evolving. In 1997 our founder Ray Dalio wrote down his lessons, starting with a Philosophy Statement which remains our foundation. This later evolved into a set of 300+ Principles. In 2022, when Ray transitioned the company, we re-underwrote several of those principles and evolved others, with a specific focus on Meritocracy. Today the culture sits, alongside our people, as our most important edge. When we get it right, it’s the engine that powers everything else. 

Explore more information about Bridgewater’s culture on our website here. 

About Your Role 

Bridgewater’s mission has always been to understand how the world works and translate that understanding into the best possible portfolios for our clients. The Client Investment Research Analyst role sits at the center of that translation. It is a role unlike others in asset management: you take Bridgewater’s view of the cause-and-effect linkages in economies and markets and put it to work advising the world’s most sophisticated institutional investors. 

You will work on the investment problems facing Bridgewater’s institutional clients: sovereign wealth funds, large public pensions, endowments, and other major allocators. The work spans the full range of what these institutions need from a macro investment partner, from synthesizing what’s going on in the world, to considering how to best manage a portfolio from the perspective of each investors’ unique goals and constraints, both strategically and tactically. You will do this alongside Bridgewater’s Strategists, a small group of senior investors appointed by our co-CIOs to lead our work with allocators; as you develop, you will take on more of the investment content those engagements carry. 

What the role builds. Over time, you develop what we call proxy CIO judgment: the ability to stand in an institutional investor’s shoes, understand their full set of constraints and objectives, and form a view on how to manage their portfolio both strategically and in view of the macro environment today. You apply Bridgewater’s macro thinking to institutional portfolios and the constraints they operate within. You also develop a working understanding of how large allocators make decisions: their governance, return objectives, liability profiles, and strategic priorities. 

Growth and career paths. Analysts progress from building foundational skills through to independent investment practitioner and, for those who continue on the team, into senior leadership roles where they operate as close partners to Strategists. At the senior end, you will hold a view on Bridgewater’s synthesis of the macro environment and portfolio construction, as well as which investment content will most change how our clients think about their portfolios. The capabilities you build here open many paths across Bridgewater’s investment community over time. The specific path depends on your strengths, interests, and how your capabilities develop.

- Designing analytical approaches to complex investment questions and executing the research from framing through synthesis

The scope spans federal, state, and local bodies in the US, EMEA and APAC — where bar associations, state licensing authorities, and judicial and legislative actions are currently setting the most consequential AI policy.
